summary:
The NASA Space Mission Design Game (SMDG) is an interactive, web-based 3D Systems Engineering and Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB) simulator built with Next.js, TypeScript, and Three.js.

What We Developed: An end-to-end mission design workbench where players architect authentic launch vehicles and satellite payloads—including Artemis SLS, Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, and James Webb-class observatories. Users balance concurrent aerospace subsystems: mass budgets, delta-V, electrical power (EPS), communications bandwidth, liftoff thrust-to-weight ratios, and real program budgets ($M), validated through live orbital trajectory simulations.

How It Addresses the Challenge: Addressing the barrier of steep, mathematical complexity in spaceflight education, SMDG translates NASA CubeSat 101 standards and JPL Horizons ephemeris data into intuitive, gamified design bays. Players directly experience aerospace trade-offs, staging mechanics, and mission debrief scoring.

Why It Is Important: SMDG democratizes space mission architecture. By bridging rigorous orbital physics with accessible, hands-on simulation, it inspires and trains the next generation of students, engineers, and flight directors to pioneer humanity's future in deep space.
details:
Project Overview & Technical Description

The NASA Space Mission Design Game (SMDG) is an interactive, browser-based 3D Systems Engineering and Vehicle Assembly simulator. Designed with an engaging voxel aesthetic, the simulator bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering principles and intuitive, hands-on learning. Players step into the role of a NASA Flight Director at a full-scale 3D launch complex and Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), where they design, construct, validate, and launch real-world spaceflight missions.

How It Works & Core Architecture

The simulator models the concurrent engineering life cycle through a unified two-stage assembly workflow:

  • Stage 1 — Launch Vehicle Architecture: Players assemble heavy-lift booster stacks, cryogenic core tanks, solid rocket boosters, upper vacuum stages, and high-thrust engine clusters. The vehicle must generate sufficient thrust to overcome atmospheric drag and achieve a safe liftoff Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR≥1.0) under aerodynamic fairing enclosures.
  • Stage 2 — Spacecraft & Payload Architecture: Players transition to the spacecraft bay to independently engineer the orbital satellite or deep-space probe. They balance onboard electrical power systems (GaAs triple-junction solar arrays and LiFePO4 battery reserves sized for orbital eclipse periods), attitude control reaction wheels, avionics flight computers, high-gain communication dishes, and scientific sensor suites.
  • Live Aerospace Physics & Budget Validation: In real time, the simulation engine calculates total dry and wet mass, delta-V (ΔV), net power balance (Wgenerated−Wconsumed​), communications link closure, and segregated multi-million-dollar program budgets.
  • Orbital Trajectory & Mission Execution: Once all pre-flight checklist gates pass, players trigger the launch sequence. The simulation tracks the vehicle from the launchpad through atmospheric Max-Q, stage staging, fairing jettison, Earth orbital insertion, and deep-space orbital transfers (such as Trans-Lunar Injection toward the Moon, Sun-Earth L2 halo insertions, and Mars-slingshot trajectories) complete with live telemetry feeds and Deep Space Network (DSN) ground tracking.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies

  • Core Stack: Built with TypeScript for strict type safety across all mathematical models and aerospace parameters, coupled with Next.js and React for seamless state management and responsive interface rendering.
  • 3D Graphics & Simulation: Powered by Three.js and WebGL, delivering real-time rendering of the 3D voxel spaceport, launchpad gantries, celestial day-and-night cycles, particle-driven rocket plumes, interactive orbital globe trajectories, and an explorable 3D component showcase gallery.
  • Interface & Motion: Styled using Tailwind CSS and Framer Motion, delivering an aerospace-grade mission control telemetry heads-up display (HUD), dynamic gauge bars, and interactive blueprint overlays.
  • Procedural Audio Synthesizer: Built on the native Web Audio API to generate real-time synthesized engine rumbles, launch countdown cues, communications chimes, and telemetry warnings dynamically in the browser without loading heavy external sound files.
  • Authentic NASA Datasets & Standards: Incorporates physical parameters from the NASA JPL Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System (planetary gravitational parameters, orbital transfer velocities, and escape speeds), the NASA CubeSat 101 Handbook, the NASA Goddard Core Flight System (cFS) architecture conventions, and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) mission data.

Creativity & Innovation

  • "Voxel Sandbox Meets Mission Control": By combining the playful, approachable familiarity of 3D block-building with rigorous aerospace physics, the platform eliminates the intimidation factor typically associated with astronautics.
  • Segregated Multi-Stage Economics: Unlike conventional space games that blend costs into a single generic score, the simulator enforces segregated financial envelopes—requiring players to budget the rocket launcher and the satellite payload independently, mirroring authentic agency procurement.
  • Interactive 3D Subsystem Showcase: Players can explore a 3D digital museum where every aerospace component—from Hall-effect xenon ion thrusters to fluxgate magnetometers—can be rotated, inspected, and studied alongside its real NASA flight heritage.
  • Inspection Tools & Fairing Cutaways: A dynamic X-ray cutaway system allows players to peel back the launch vehicle's payload fairings to reveal the delicate spacecraft packaged inside, emphasizing volumetric constraints and acoustic isolation.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Hands-on Systems Thinking: Teaches students and space enthusiasts that no engineering decision happens in isolation. Adding a heavier scientific camera increases spacecraft mass, which demands larger batteries, heavier structural support, larger rocket boosters, and increased budget allocations.
  • Democratizing Space Education: Provides students, educators, and university engineering programs worldwide with free, frictionless access to NASA-level mission planning directly in any modern web browser.
  • Workforce Inspiration: Sparks curiosity and equips the next generation of scientists, systems engineers, and flight directors by faithfully recreating iconic missions such as Artemis I (SLS / Orion), Sentinel-6 (Falcon 9), Psyche (Falcon Heavy), and the James Webb Space Telescope (Ariane 5 ECA).

Design Considerations & Engineering Trade-Offs

  • Authenticity vs. Accessibility: While equations for thrust-to-weight ratios, orbital velocity, and battery eclipse depletion are mathematically genuine, they are communicated through clear, color-coded telemetry gauges and actionable pre-flight diagnostic checklists rather than impenetrable walls of math.
  • Real Aerospace Capitalization: Replaced artificial "experience points" with real-world aerospace financial figures ($M), teaching players the fiscal discipline required in modern space exploration.
  • Adaptive Difficulty Tiers: Designed scalable difficulty profiles—ranging from Cadet (generous margins and lower thrust requirements for beginners) to Engineer (standard NASA baseline margins) and Flight Director (strict tolerances and tighter budget constraints).
  • Hardware Inclusivity: Optimized procedural textures and 3D geometries to ensure smooth 60 FPS performance on standard classroom laptops and Chromebooks without requiring high-end dedicated gaming hardware.
